data.name: Muayyad
data.gender_notes: Muayyad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'Awwa' meaning 'to help'. Muayyad refers to someone who is supported or helped, or someone who helps and supports others. In Islamic history, Muayyad is the name of several scholars and Sufi saints who were renowned for their knowledge, wisdom, and spiritual guidance. The name Muayyad carries the meaning “Helped or supported” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muayyad usually hope their child will grow to embody helped or supported and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes support, guidance, and spiritual nourishment.
data.etymology: Muayyad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Helped or supported.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muayyad total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

The name Muayyad is derived from the Arabic root 'ayyada', which means 'to support' or 'to strengthen'. The name Muayyad is also associated with the qualities of strength, courage, and determination, making it a popular choice for parents seeking to instill these values in their children.

historical_references.reference: Muayyad al-Din al-Shirazi was a Persian astronomer and mathematician. He wrote an astronomical work known as the 'Zij-e Jadid' or 'New Astronomy', which is considered the most important Islamic work in this field after the works of Al-Biruni and Al-Khwarizmi. The work was completed around 1079 CE in Shiraz, Persia.
historical_references.context: Persian astronomer and mathematician, author of 'Zij-e Jadid' (New Astronomy)

historical_references.reference: Muayyad al-Din al-Shamsi was a renowned Islamic scholar, theologian, and jurist from Damascus, Syria, who is best known for his work 'Al-I'tisam' (The Protection), a classic work on Islamic law and ethics. It was written around 1276 CE during the Mamluk Sultanate in Egypt and Syria.
